decision_scope: Literature- and Core-contract screen of candidate finite-temperature condensed response schemes; not admission of a physical He-II operator
what_is_closed: No currently inspected scheme can be inherited as an admitted UET He-II second-sound operator. A single-charge UET-action derivation is the first bounded technical attempt; external two-fluid methods remain comparators.
equation_or_mapping: h(p; protocol) = detector[longitudinal_response(source; stationary_condensed_UET_state(p))] is undefined until the state, currents and source/detector map are derived in one declared scheme
units: UET O(2) calculations are natural-unit; the He-II response requires an independent material/SI map
observable: He-II longitudinal thermal response or second-sound speed with matched excitation/readout protocol
claim_boundary: A route-selection decision, not an impossibility theorem, physical second-sound prediction, independent validation, or Full Topic 13 closure

primary_sources.relevance: Symmetry-improved O(2) CJT equilibrium Goldstone and phase-transition construction
Semi-rigorous and numerical evidence for solution loss in a two-loop O(2) symmetry-improved scheme; not a universal no-go theorem
Two-chemical-potential HFB EOS and two-fluid hydrodynamic mapping in a different model
Two-fluid sound depends on superfluid density, thermodynamics and probe coupling; model/medium differences matter

candidate_routes.reason: Formal leading auxiliary-field/large-N-inspired lane, Z>1 domain, no controlled microscopic 2PI/1N, normal two-fluid response or SI material map; frozen Z=1 state cannot be reused
Fixed reference conditions permit different finite local counterterms with different stationary-point behavior; physical prescription not selected
Declared implementation is restricted to mu=0 and is not a condensed finite-density longitudinal response
Equilibrium Goldstone property does not settle reported linear-response overdetermination or scheme existence at the required finite-T and finite-density UET state
Introduces an additional chemical-potential prescription and model-specific Bose-gas EOS; charge/ensemble correspondence to declared single-charge UET action is unproved
Provides a reference longitudinal response when material inputs are supplied but cannot derive UET superfluid density, normal dynamics, transport or Phi response

selected_next_question: Can a single-charge, fixed-prescription finite-T condensed response be derived from the declared UET action with joint stationarity, Ward identity and nonzero longitudinal source coupling, without using target sound data?
admission_requirements: Declare the UET action, single conserved charge and renormalization prescription once for all states
Solve joint Phi, condensate and gap stationarity on a stable bounded finite-temperature domain
Check the O(2) Ward identity and equilibrium thermodynamic derivative consistency
Derive charge, entropy and momentum currents and their linearized longitudinal conservation/balance equations
Specify excitation, detector, geometry, units and independent material state map before target comparison
Prove finite response and convergence, or record a scoped obstruction with an explicit assumption class
stop_rule: At the D5 science-route decision, if joint state and source-coupled longitudinal operator are not admitted, report G1/G2 UNRESOLVED and use a methods/measurement-feasibility portfolio; do not generate a second-sound score by importing comparator coefficients
next_action: Derive or refute the single-charge source-coupled longitudinal response in one declared finite-T condensed UET scheme; seek Core-owner review before changing Core equations
